title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continuing pp. 193 and 195): Grothendieck is working in the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets'. A point x of a twisted moduli object M_{0,3}^{!~} gives quantities f, g, h, α0, β0, α, β, ξ, η in the profinite fundamental group Π^_{0,3} of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}. α0 and α lie only in the extension Π^~_{0,3} = Π^_{0,3}·{1,τ0}. These data encode a Galois or GT-type automorphism together with its 'loop equation'.

In §III he pushes everything into GL(2,Ẑ)' = GL(2,Ẑ)/±1. The map is through the identification Π_{0,3} ≅ Γ(2)/±1, with the generators l0 = (1 2; 0 1) and l1 = (1 0; 2 1). Determinants:
- det α0 = det α = ε3, where ε3 ≡ χ mod 3 and χ is the cyclotomic character.
- All the other quantities lie in SL(2,Ẑ)'.

One chooses lifts f, α0, β0 in GL(2,Ẑ), which amounts to choosing three signs. On this page he defines the remaining quantities from these choices (system (59)):
- ξ = α ρ(α)^{-1} and η = β ρ_∞(β)^{-1}, where ρ, ρ_∞ are the automorphisms induced by permutations of {0,1,∞}, realized as conjugations in GL2;
- α0 = f^{-1} α and β0 = f^{-1} β;
- g = α0 ρ(α0)^{-1} = f^{-1} ξ ρ(f) and h = β0 ρ(β0)^{-1} = f^{-1} η ρ(f).

He notes that ξ, η, g, h do not depend on the sign choices. This holds because ±1 is central and fixed by the conjugations ρ, ρ_∞, so the sign cancels in α ρ(α)^{-1}.

The essential relation, besides the defining relations (59), is the matrix form of the 'relation des lacets', corresponding to his earlier (43)/(46): ξ = ε η l1^ν, with ε ∈ {±1}. The sign ε no longer depends on any choice: ε = ε2, where μ ≡ ε2 mod 4. Since l1^ν = (1 0; 2ν 1) = (1 0; μ−1 1) (next page), μ = 2ν+1 plays the role of the GT parameter λ = 2m+1 attached to χ.

So the page computes the image of the Ihara/GT 'loop (hexagon) relation' in the congruence quotient (Γ(2) inside SL2(Ẑ)), where it holds up to a canonical sign. That sign is fixed by μ mod 4, just as det α is fixed by χ mod 3. The purpose is a concrete matrix model in which the unknown f can be explicitly computed or tested. The next page relates these notations to those of §44 (pp. 356 ff.).
errors: Notational inconsistency: η is defined with ρ_∞ (η = β ρ_∞(β)^{-1}), but h is written as β0 ρ(β0)^{-1} = f^{-1} η ρ(f). For h to be the analogue of η, it should presumably use ρ_∞ throughout: β0 ρ_∞(β0)^{-1} = f^{-1} η ρ_∞(f). The crossed-out version used σ_∞ for h, which shows the hesitation.
The crossed-out first draft had β0 = f β0 (a typo); Grothendieck corrected it to β0 = f^{-1} β.
The algebra checks out: α0 ρ(α0)^{-1} = f^{-1} α ρ(α)^{-1} ρ(f) = f^{-1} ξ ρ(f).
The claim that ε = ε2 (μ ≡ ε2 mod 4) is quoted from earlier computations and not re-proved here.

ideas.what: Mapping the GT/Galois data (f and its cocycle relations) on π1(P^1−{0,1,∞}) into the congruence completion via Π_{0,3} ≅ Γ(2)/±1 inside PSL2(Ẑ)/PGL2(Ẑ), with l0, l1 as generators.
ideas.modern_name: Congruence (Legendre-family) quotient of the GT action; Galois action on torsion of the Legendre elliptic curve
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara (Galois action on the fundamental group of P^1−3 points, 1980s); Nakamura, Ihara–Matsumoto on related congruence quotients
ideas.where_published: Not in the Esquisse in this form; the Longue Marche (1981) works with Π_{0,3}^ and Teichmüller-type actions.

ideas.what: Defining 'cocycle' quantities ξ = α ρ(α)^{-1} (twisting by order-3/order-2 symmetries) and showing they are independent of sign lifts.
ideas.modern_name: Coboundary of a lift under the S3-symmetry; the 2-cycle and 3-cycle relations of GT
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara (1991) for the GT relations

ideas.what: Matrix form of the loop relation ξ = ε η l1^ν with a canonical sign ε determined by μ mod 4 (μ = 2ν+1), and det α determined by χ mod 3.
ideas.modern_name: Image of the hexagon relation f(x,y) x^m f(z,x) z^m f(y,z) y^m = 1 (m = (λ−1)/2) in PGL2(Ẑ), with sign corrections
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld/Ihara for the relation; sign bookkeeping in GL2 lift not standardly attributed

missed.claim: Explicit bookkeeping of the signs when lifting the GT/Galois loop relation from PSL2(Ẑ) to GL2(Ẑ): ε = ε2 with μ ≡ ε2 mod 4, and det = ε3 with χ mod 3. This is a small concrete detail, apparently not written down this way in the literature, though easily rederivable.
missed.quote: ξ = ε η l^ν  ... où ε est un signe qui ne dépend plus d'aucun choix ... ε = ε2, μ ≡ ε2 (4)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor: useful for anyone computing the image of GT in congruence quotients or comparing GT with SL2/modular actions. Otherwise mainly of historical interest, showing that Grothendieck pre-dated Drinfeld's GT relations in matrix form.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but routine computation inside Grothendieck's pre-Drinfeld development of the loop equation, projected to Γ(2) inside PGL2(Ẑ). It is historically interesting as evidence of his GT-type relations around 1981–82, but the content (relations and signs) is elementary and largely implicit in later work by Ihara, Drinfeld and others.
transcription_corrections: In (60), the boxed relation should read ξ = ε η l1^ν (the matrix l1 = (1 0; 2 1) defined on the next page), not ξ = ε η h^ν. The next page's 'où l1 est défini matriciellement' and its formula (48) ξ = η l1^ν confirm this.
The first line of (59) reads η = β ρ_∞(β)^{-1} (the subscript ∞ is written below ρ), consistent with the transcription.
In the crossed-out block, the second line reads α0 = f^{-1}α, β0 = f β0 (an erroneous draft).
